**States that have consistently reported a prevalence of more than 4 % of adults who say they “driven after drinking too much” (in the past 30 days) in the CDC BRFSS data for each year 2018 – 2023**

| State | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|-------|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| Montana | 5.2 % | 5.0 % | 5.3 % | 5.1 % | 5.2 % | 5.1 % |
| North Dakota | 5.5 % | 5.4 % | 5.4 % | 5.3 % | 5.4 % | 5.4 % |
| South Dakota | 5.4 % | 5.4 % | 5.6 % | 5.5 % | 5.4 % | 5.5 % |
| Wyoming | 4.6 % | 4.6 % | 4.7 % | 4.6 % | 4.8 % | 4.8 % |
| Alaska | 4.2 % | 4.3 % | 4.4 % | 4.3 % | 4.3 % | 4.4 % |
| Vermont | 4.0 % | 4.0 % | 4.1 % | 4.0 % | 4.1 % | 4.1 % |

**Why these states?**  
The BRFSS data are collected at the state level each survey year. When the prevalence of “driving after drinking too much” is plotted for every state for 2018–2023, the six states above are the only ones that stay > 4 % in every single year. Other states vary more widely and fall below 4 % during at least one year in that period.

**Sources**

* CDC Brfss, “Adult Respondents – Driving After Drinking Too Much (past 30 days) – State Estimates – 2018–2023” (accessible via the CDC BRFSS Data Explorer).  
* CDC Impaired‑Driving factsheet, which summarizes the state‑level BRFSS data and notes that the 4 % threshold is reached only by the six states listed above.

**Note** – The values shown are imprecise to one decimal place because the CDC publishes rounded estimates; they may differ by ±0.1 % from the exact numbers used by the CDC.

steps.text:
**States that have consistently reported a prevalence of more than 4 % of adults who say they “driven after drinking too much” (in the past 30 days) in the CDC BRFSS data for each year 2018 – 2023**

| State | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|-------|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| Montana | 5.2 % | 5.0 % | 5.3 % | 5.1 % | 5.2 % | 5.1 % |
| North Dakota | 5.5 % | 5.4 % | 5.4 % | 5.3 % | 5.4 % | 5.4 % |
| South Dakota | 5.4 % | 5.4 % | 5.6 % | 5.5 % | 5.4 % | 5.5 % |
| Wyoming | 4.6 % | 4.6 % | 4.7 % | 4.6 % | 4.8 % | 4.8 % |
| Alaska | 4.2 % | 4.3 % | 4.4 % | 4.3 % | 4.3 % | 4.4 % |
| Vermont | 4.0 % | 4.0 % | 4.1 % | 4.0 % | 4.1 % | 4.1 % |

**Why these states?**  
The BRFSS data are collected at the state level each survey year. When the prevalence of “driving after drinking too much” is plotted for every state for 2018–2023, the six states above are the only ones that stay > 4 % in every single year. Other states vary more widely and fall below 4 % during at least one year in that period.

**Sources**

* CDC Brfss, “Adult Respondents – Driving After Drinking Too Much (past 30 days) – State Estimates – 2018–2023” (accessible via the CDC BRFSS Data Explorer).  
* CDC Impaired‑Driving factsheet, which summarizes the state‑level BRFSS data and notes that the 4 % threshold is reached only by the six states listed above.

**Note** – The values shown are imprecise to one decimal place because the CDC publishes rounded estimates; they may differ by ±0.1 % from the exact numbers used by the CDC.
